b: People are making death threats telling me to write the next chapter.. so I trust at least a few of you liked it..so I'll write as much as I can

There can't be anyone living in Wellawatte who doesn't know Visa Pillaiyar.. For the new generation he's IBC Pillaiyar. He gets that name because he sits there elegantly at the end of IBC Lane, looking at the sea. But during the war, people would make a vow here before going abroad.. and they'd get the visa too.. and the people who worship there get lots of modakam and aval.. Even though fewer people come asking for visas now, Pillaiyar's popularity among the old-timers hasn't dropped.

I went with half-hearted faith, dropped 50 rupees and prayed..maybe that's why, when the next day it came back wrong again, I nearly went mad. It was Mithra who applied for the visa again, saying send it once more ..Meanwhile, three of them had their flight that day.. (You'll ask what happened to the fourth.. I'll tell you in detail later) The three of them went off to catch the night flight. I had book work at a friend's house that night, so I was there working

At the airport, too, the Vietnamese guy dropped another bomb.. He'd typed the date wrong on one of our guys' visa.. So the airline guy said he wouldn't let him in..They pleaded and begged and tried everything.. He wouldn't budge at all.. Then what to do.. When he called us and told us the story, we were sad and laughing at the same time.. Leaving him behind, the other two set off. He came home, thinking he'd go to the embassy next day and try something

His name is Dhanush.. he was at school with me… but we only really got close after going to campus.. I asked him before writing about him..He said, just don't tell any lies. So everything I say is true.. A really good guy.. He doesn't talk unnecessarily.. But he's read a lot.. He talks deeply about lots of things.. His thinking is all different..that's why, even though he was upset about missing the flight, he didn't make a fuss and decided straight away what to do next

Next morning he called and asked if I was coming to the embassy; I had only just got up.. I told him I was too broke to come, and thought I'd check my mail anyway, and there was my visa.. After the drama that happened to him, I checked every date four times over and announced it to the whole town, and his visa got sorted out somehow too.

That's when everyone understood Visa Pillaiyar's power.. He gave me the visa and also stopped someone getting on a plane so he could go with me as company. He did lose a bit of money.. Don't ask how much.. If I tell you in rupees it'll hurt his heart.. But profit and loss isn't all there is to life, see.. so let's leave it
Then they scrambled and booked a flight for the two of us together.. I bought medicines, pills, clothes, everything, and the two of us set off to catch the Saturday night flight
But there too, a seven-and-a-half had gathered and was waiting
note: The chapter title, "Pillaiyar suzhi", is the curl Tamils write at the top of a page for a lucky start. Modakam and aval (sweet dumplings and rice flakes) are offerings to Ganesha. A "seven-and-a-half" (ēḻarai) is the seven-and-a-half-year spell of bad luck that Saturn brings in astrology; in everyday speech it means trouble.
